nodes.source_text: Second, Zn–NiFeP/CC was obtained by phosphorylation in an Ar atmosphere.

nodes.name: Selective Zn acid etching
nodes.procedure: d-NiFeP/CC with abundant defects was obtained by selective acid etching of Zn atoms in the Zn–NiFeP/CC precursor. As reported in previous studies, both Ni and Zn are divalent cations and the Zn atom will occupy the position of the Ni atom. Therefore, after acid etching of Zn atoms, it is easier for the Ni atoms near the Zn atoms to have defects than Fe atoms in Zn–NiFeP/CC.
nodes.source_text: Finally, NiFeP/CC with abundant defects (d-NiFeP/CC) was obtained by a selective etching method... after acid etching of Zn atoms, it is easier for the Ni atoms near the Zn atoms to have defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks of d-NiFeP/CC match well with Ni2P phase, indicating nickel iron bimetallic phosphides phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S2b,† the diffraction peaks of the d-NiFeP/CC pre-catalyst match well with the Ni2P phase...

nodes.characterization_summary: d-NiFeP shows array structure uniformly grown on CC with mass loading of 5.46 mg cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A scanning electron microscope (SEM) was used to observe the morphology of d-NiFeP/CC (Fig. 1b). The d-NiFeP shows an array structure...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni and Fe contents in d-NiFeP/CC are 15.18 wt% and 5.12 wt%, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The chemical compositions of the prepared Zn–NiFeP/CC and d-NiFeP/CC were accurately analyzed by using inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni, Fe and P elements are uniformly distributed on the sheet structure of d-NiFeP/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1c, Ni, Fe and P elements are uniformly distributed on the sheet structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: d-NiFeP/CC shows thin sheet with interconnected pieces, exposed edges, amorphous regions wrapped by crystalline regions, and lattice fringes of 0.167 nm corresponding to (211) plane of (NiFe)2P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: d-NiFeP/CC shows a thin sheet consisting of many interconnected pieces and exposed edges (Fig. 1g)... lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 0.167 nm, corresponding to the (211) plane of (NiFe)2P.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of d-NiFeP/CC is 11.4 m^2 g^-1, higher than NiFeP/CC (3.9 m^2 g^-1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: By measuring the nitrogen adsorption–desorption isothermal curves... the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area of d-NiFeP/CC was 11.4 m^2 g^-1 which was higher than that of NiFeP/CC (3.9 m^2 g^-1).

nodes.characterization_summary: d-NiFeP/CC shows Ni 2p main peak at 853.8 eV (Ni–P), peaks at 857.1 and 875.2 eV, Fe 2p peaks at 712.4 and 725.2 eV, peak at 708.1 eV (Fe–P), P 2p peaks at 129.6, 130.5 eV (P-M) and 133.9 eV (P-O); binding energies positively shifted by 0.6-0.8 eV compared to NiFeP/CC indicating defects and increased metal valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p spectrum, the main peak at 853.8 eV after deconvolution corresponds to Ni–P... peaks of Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 are located at 712.4 and 725.2 eV... peak at 708.1 eV... attributed to Fe-P... The P 2p spectra of d-NiFeP/CC show three peaks at 129.6, 130.5 and 133.9 eV... The binding energy of Ni for d-NiFeP/CC is positively shifted by 0.6 and 0.7 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER, d-NiFeP/CC shows polycrystalline disordered NiOOH structure with lattice fringes of 0.208 nm (NiOOH (201)) and FFT diffraction rings of NiOOH (210)/(310).
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-TEM images confirm that the NiOOH generation from the d-NiFeP/CC pre-catalyst surface reconstruction is a polycrystalline disordered structure... lattice fringes with a plane spacing of 0.208 nm... corresponding to the (201) crystal plane of NiOOH.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface reconstruction of the d-NiFeP/CC pre-catalyst was monitored by in situ Raman spectroscopy... two Raman peaks appeared at 478 cm^-1 and 578 cm^-1, which correspond to the bending vibration of Eg(δ(Ni-O)) and the stretching vibration of A1g(ν(Ni-O)) in NiOOH.
